title: Functions Basics
code:
def main():
    kids = int(input("How many kids? "))
    apples = int(input("How many apples? "))
    rounds = 0
    while apples >= kids:
        apples -= kids
        rounds += 1
    print(apples, "apples left after round", rounds)
    print("Each kid got {0} apples.".format(rounds))
    print("{0} apples left.".format(apples))

lines.explanation: Taking number of kids as an integer input from the user
Taking number of apples as an integer input from the user
Initiating the variable 'rounds' (assigning the value '0'). This variable will be used as the counter for number of rounds
This while loop will iterate till the condition 'apples is greater than or equal to kids' is true.
decrementing the value of apples by number of kids in each iteration (round)
incrementing the value of 'rounds' by 1 to denote the 'number of rounds'
This will print out 'x' number of apples left after 'y' rounds. Here x and y are integer values that are computed in the While loop

This print statement uses the concept of output formatting. Here the value of 'rounds' is passed within the print statement by using the 'format' method and passing the argument 'rounds'. Here '0' stands for the index number of the argument tuple. 'rounds' is passed as the first argument (index 0) so {0} would fetch the value of 'rounds'

Here we print the number of apples left at the end. Again, here {0} represents the index number of the variable in the tuple. Index 0 has the variable apples. Hence the value of apples will be printed out within the print statement.
